newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.

text.p: WOMEN UNHAPPY WITH ABORTION MOVE
The Women's Electoral Lobby says a right-wing agenda to drive women
back into the home and make them work for nothing, won't happen..
The W.E.L's Jo Wainer, was commenting on a push by Independent No text received
Senator Brian Harradine for an end to medicare-funded abortions,
funding of family planning clinics and rebates for in-vitro
fertilisation.
Ms Wainer says the Coaltion has already cut support for child care
and there'll be enormous resistance to a deal between the
Government and Senator Harradine.
Federal Health Minister Michael Wooldridge has confirmed he has
held talks with Senator Harradine.
The government needs his vote to get the Telstra bill and other key
legislation through the Senate.
SALVOS WARNING ON UNEMPLOYMENT
The Salvation Army has warned Government reforms to labour market
programs will create an underclass.
Salvation Army Captain, David Eldridge, says the long term
unemployed will be marginalised and abandoned if they don't have
the opportunity to participate in a labour market program.
He says such programs keep unemployed people connected to the
community.
People who train and support the jobless are worried the new
"benefit test" will exclude people from labour market programs and
lead to less disadvantaged jobseekers receiving more attention.
PADDLESTEAMER PASSENGERS RESCUED
Nearly 80 passengers were ferried ashore from a paddelsteamer on
the Murray River late last night, after the vessel ran aground for
a second time on the same trip.
The Cumberoona set out from Albury yesterday morning with 79
passengers on board and ran aground on a sand bar in the late
afternoon.
After about six hours, the crew freed the cruiser but it ran
aground again on the return journey.
A passenger called for help on a mobile phone.
The passengers were ferried ashore and taken by buses to Albury,
while the boat was freed again.
INQUIRY INTO AUSTRALIAN FEDERAL POLICE OPENS
The head of an inquiry into allegations of corruption in the
Australian Federal Police says there're likely to be both closed
and public hearings.
Ian Harrison will consider written material in private over the
next two weeks, before deciding whether to hold public hearings.
The inquiry, opening in Sydney today, has been sparked by a former
officer's allegations of corruption in the A.F.P, mainly in
relation to drug deals in the 1970s and 80s.
Alan Taciak says he can name nearly 80 corrupt officers
BORBIDGE THREATENS EARLY ELECTION
Queensland Premier, Rob Borbidge, says a snap election remains an
option if reforms to the State's Workers' Compensation Scheme are
blocked in Parliament.
The scheme is more than 400 million dollars in the red.
Independent MP, Liz Cunningham, who holds the balance of power,
says she can't support provisions limiting injured workers' access
to the courts.
Mr Borbidge says those provisions are not negotiable.
He says if the reform package is blocked, the Government's options
are a snap poll or to close down the scheme, leaving Queensland
without workers' compensation.
BISHOP URGES VOTE AGAINST EUTHANASIA
The Anglican Archbishop of Sydney, Harry Goodhew, says the Northern
Territory's voluntary euthanasia legislation affects the whole
country, and it's appropriate for Federal legislation to overturn
it.
Federal Liberal back bencher, Kevin Andrews, is scheduled today to
deliver the second reading of his private members bill, which would
effectively overturn the law.
Archbishop Goodhew is urging members of parliament to think of the
kind of society there want to leave their children, when they vote
on the anti-euthanasia bill.
He says legalising euthanasia breaches the historic protection of
human life.
HIGH COST FOR CAREER WOMEN
A national businesswomen's conference in Hobart has been told that
most women who reach the top in their profession pay a high
personal cost for career advancement.
The Australian Federation of Business and Professional Women's
conference has heard that many women are unrealistically pressured
to aspire to the glamorous image of a "super-woman".
The University of Tasmania's Joan Abbott-Chapman warns that
burnouts, accidents and even suicides result from a growing
imbalance between the demands on women.
Associate Professor Abbott-Chapman says her research shows that a
rising number of rural women are having accidents on the farm as
they take on more labouring jobs in the rural recession.
HARRADINE WANTS MEDICARE FUNDED ABORTIONS SCRAPPED
A push by Independent Senator Brian Harradine to scrap
Medicare-funded abortions and end payments to family planning
clinics, is being resisted by the Federal Opposition and the
Democrats.
Senator Harradine's wish list reportedly also includes the
scrapping of rebates for in-vitro fertilisation.
Democrats Leader, Cheryl Kernot, has joined the Opposition in
saying they shouldn't be the subject of political horse-trading.
The Government refusing to be drawn on how seriously the proposals
are being considered.
